gaps.requirement: T2 'Decide whether an app supports a particular image type' (benchmark 5; section 1 rows 'Will it work with my images or data?' and 'What will I get out of it?'; section 4 'inputs, outputs, limitations, example data ... live in the app repository and feed the website automatically')
gaps.current: FAIL. The page text never states an input format, dimensionality, output or limitation. CellTracksColab page (usab3/t2-celltrackscolab-full.png) says only 'compiles tracking results (for example from TrackMate)'; VLab4Mic says 'Build virtual samples from molecular structures...' (no formats, no outputs); NucleiSky says '2D and 3D' but not that pixel size metadata is mandatory. The facts exist upstream only on GitHub: CellTracksColab README:152-158 'Required File Format: CSV or XML files' and :246 test datasets on Zenodo; NucleiSky README:79-82 'Pixel and Voxel size matter immensely ... alignment fails' and docs/limitations.md. The schema (schema/labconstrictor-app.schema.json) has only schema,name,summary,description,quickstart,kind,hosts,distribution,authors,license,categories,doi,homepage,docs_url,icon,screenshots: no inputs, outputs, limitations or example_data field, so a visitor must open GitHub. Also 5 of 6 apps have 0 screenshots in build/snapshot.json and NucleiSky's only 'screenshot' is a banner.jpg captioned 'NucleiSky banner.' (no input/output example).
gaps.proposal: Add four optional-then-required manifest fields: inputs (list of short strings: format + dimensionality), outputs (list), limitations (list), example_data (list of {label,url}). Render them in pages_apps as 'Works with' and 'Produces' directly under the lead sentence and a 'Limitations' block lower down (esc()-escaped, no markdown); add inputs/outputs text to cards.search_text so search matches data types; make inputs+outputs required in validate.py for any app not in section testing (explicit error naming the app, no silent default); change the 'screenshots' rule to required for non-testing apps. The facts come from each app's labconstrictor-app.yaml, so no second description is kept in the site.
gaps.rule_conflicts: none; matches the 'authors expose only what they choose' and single-source-of-truth rules. New code must stay <=30 lines per function and pages_apps.py is already 208 lines, so put the new section in a new module to keep files <=300. Fields must be added to the template and the initialiser form (LabConstrictor_streamlit) so authors are asked for them.

gaps.current: FAIL, contradictory signals. On /apps/ the filter is labelled 'WORKS IN' and selecting napari returns 3 apps (Guess the Condition, VLab4Mic, LabConstrictor Playground), each carrying the chip 'Soon in napari' (usab3/t5-01-filter-napari.png). On /apps/labconstrictor-vlab4mic/ the badge says 'Soon in napari', the About text says 'Two of its tools also run in Napari and Fiji', and Details has the row 'Works in: napari, Fiji' (usab3/t5-02-vlab4mic-fold.png). gaps.proposal: Change hosts entries to objects {host: napari|fiji|qupath, status: planned|experimental|usable, tools: [names], tested_with: 'napari 0.5.x'} (the manifest owns the fact), render the chip text from status ('Experimental in napari', 'Planned: napari'), rename the filter to 'Also in' (or filter on status != planned) and replace the Details row 'Works in' with 'napari: experimental (tools X, Y; tested with ...)'. Remove the 'also run in Napari' sentence from the VLab4Mic description in its own repo, or make it agree.

unverified: Real Apple hardware, Safari and Chrome-under-Rosetta were not tested: the Apple Silicon/Intel emulation overrides Chromium client hints through CDP (architecture arm/x86) and removes userAgentData to simulate Safari/Firefox. Whether a real Chrome under Rosetta reports x86 on an M-series Mac (and therefore promotes the wrong button) is not verified.

Installer files were not downloaded (303 MB each, GitHub is outside the sandbox); I verified only the hrefs and the sizes in build/snapshot.json, so I did not see whether the .pkg/.exe actually launch, nor the real SmartScreen/Gatekeeper prompts.

The header (Zensical) search returned no results for 'nuclei segmentation' in the preview server; I did not establish whether its index is simply not built or not loaded under the python http.server preview, so I make no claim about it beyond that.
I did not check whether the release asset API supplies SHA-256 digests (G5c); that proposal depends on it.

T3/T4 were run at 1280 px desktop only for the Mac and Windows UAs; on phone I tested a Chrome/Mac UA with keyboard and a Chrome/Linux default, not a real iOS Safari (where lcSystem() returns null for iPhone/iPad, so no 'YOUR SYSTEM' tile is marked).

The NucleiSky clone in /home/user has no labconstrictor-app.yaml; the manifest facts above come from build/snapshot.json (fetched from GitHub), not from the local clone, and the manifest of the upstream repo was not re-read.
